bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 孝惠皇帝諱衷，字正度，武帝第二子也。

translations.literal: The Filial and Kind Emperor, taboo name Zhong, courtesy name Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui, whose personal name was Sima Zhong and courtesy name Zhengdu, was Emperor Wu’s second son.

sentences.zh: 泰始三年，立爲皇太子，時年九歲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi, he was established as crown prince; at the time he was nine sui.
translations.idiomatic: In 267, when he was nine years old, he was named heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taixi, on the jiyou day of the fourth month, Emperor Wu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on the day jiyou, Emperor Wu died.

sentences.zh: 是日，皇太子即皇帝位，大赦，改元爲永熙。

translations.literal: That same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxi.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the heir apparent ascended the throne, ordered a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Yongxi.

sentences.zh: 尊皇后楊氏曰皇太后，立妃賈氏爲皇后。

translations.literal: The empress, Lady Yang, was honored as empress dowager; Consort Jia was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang was elevated to empress dowager, and his consort Lady Jia was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，歲星晝見。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the year star was seen in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter shone visible in broad daylight during the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 冏將何勖、盧播擊張泓於陽翟，大破之，斬孫輔等。

translations.literal: Jiong’s generals He Xu and Lu Bo attacked Zhang Hong at Yangzhai, greatly defeated him, and beheaded Sun Fu and others.
translations.idiomatic: He Xu and Lu Bo, under Prince Jiong, crushed Zhang Hong at Yangzhai and executed Sun Fu among others.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，左衛將軍王輿與尚書、淮陵王漼勒兵入宮，禽倫黨孫秀、孫會、許超、士猗、駱休等，皆斬之。

translations.literal: On the xinyou day, General of the Left Guards Wang Yu, together with the minister, Prince Cui of Huailing, led troops into the palace, captured Lun’s faction Sun Xiu, Sun Hui, Xu Chao, Shi Yi, Luo Xiu, and others; all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day Wang Yu and Prince Cui of Huailing forced the palace gates, seized Lun’s confederates Sun Xiu, Sun Hui, Xu Chao, Shi Yi, Luo Xiu, and others, and put them all to the sword.

sentences.zh: 逐倫歸第，即日乘輿反正。

translations.literal: They expelled Lun to return to his residence; that same day the imperial carriage returned to rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lun was sent home under guard, and the emperor was restored to the throne that same day.

sentences.zh: 群臣頓首謝罪，帝曰：「非諸卿之過也。」

translations.literal: The host of ministers knocked their heads in admitting guilt; the emperor said, “It is not the fault of you various ministers.”
translations.idiomatic: The ministers prostrated themselves in apology, but the emperor told them, “None of this was your doing.”

sentences.zh: 癸亥，詔曰：「朕以不德，纂承皇統，遠不能光濟大業，靖綏四方；

translations.literal: On the guihai day, an edict stated: “I, lacking virtue, have succeeded to the imperial line; afar I have been unable to brighten and aid the great enterprise and pacify and soothe the four directions;
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day an edict began: “Lacking virtue, I yet inherited the throne, and I have not been able to extend the great enterprise or bring peace to the four quarters of the realm;

sentences.zh: 近不能開明刑威，式遏姦宄，至使逆臣孫秀敢肆凶虐，窺間王室，遂奉趙王倫饕據天位。

translations.literal: Near I have been unable to open and clarify punishments and might and check villainy and treachery, so that the rebellious minister Sun Xiu dared unleash cruelty and violence, spy on and divide the royal house, and thereupon supporting Prince Lun of Zhao greedily seized the heavenly position.
translations.idiomatic: Near at hand I failed to make law and majesty clear enough to stop treason, so the rebel Sun Xiu could brutalize the court, tear at the royal house, and help Prince Lun of Zhao seize the throne by force.

sentences.zh: 鎮東大將軍、齊王冏，征北大將軍、成都王穎，征西大將軍、河間王顒，並以明德茂親，忠規允著，首建大策，匡救國難。

translations.literal: General-in-chief who guards the east, Prince Jiong of Qi; general-in-chief who conquers the north, Prince Ying of Chengdu; general-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Yong of Hejian—all with bright virtue as flourishing kin, loyal plans truly manifest, first established the great strategy and rectified and saved the state’s crisis.
translations.idiomatic: General-in-chief who guards the east Prince Jiong of Qi, general-in-chief who conquers the north Prince Ying of Chengdu, and general-in-chief who conquers the west Prince Yong of Hejian are men of shining virtue and eminent kinship whose loyal counsel stood the test; they first devised the great plan that delivered the state from disaster.

sentences.zh: 尚書漼共立大謀，左衛將軍王輿與群公卿士，協同謀略，親勒本營，斬秀及其二子。

translations.literal: Minister Cui together established the great plan; General of the Left Guards Wang Yu, together with the host of dukes, ministers, and gentlemen, coordinated in stratagem, personally commanded the original camp, and beheaded Xiu and his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Cui framed the decisive plot; Wang Yu, general of the left guards, with the high ministers acting in concert, led their household troops into the palace and slew Sun Xiu together with his two sons.

sentences.zh: 前趙王倫爲秀所誤，與其子等已詣金墉迎朕幽宮，旋軫閶闔。

translations.literal: The former Prince Lun of Zhao was misled by Xiu; together with his sons and others he had already gone to Jinyong to welcome me from the hidden palace, turning the carriage at Changhe.
translations.idiomatic: The former Prince Lun of Zhao was deceived by Sun Xiu; he and his sons had already reached the Jinyong compound to bring me out of confinement and were turning their carriages toward the Changhe Gate.

sentences.zh: 豈在予一人獨饗其慶，宗廟社稷實有賴焉。」

translations.literal: How could it be that I alone partake of the blessing? The ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain truly have relied on this.”
translations.idiomatic: How could the blessing rest on me alone? The ancestral shrines and the altars of soil and grain have truly depended on them.”

sentences.zh: 於是大赦，改元，孤寡賜穀五斛，大酺五日。

translations.literal: Thereupon a general amnesty; the era name was changed; widowers, widows, and orphans were granted grain, five hu; great feasting for five days.
translations.idiomatic: With the edict closed, the court ordered a general amnesty, a new reign title, five hu of grain for every widow, widower, and orphan, and five days of public feasting.

sentences.zh: 誅趙王倫、義陽王威、九門侯質等及倫之黨與。

translations.literal: Prince Lun of Zhao, Prince Wei of Yiyang, Marquis Zhi of Jiumen, and others, and Lun’s factional followers, were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lun, Prince Wei of Yiyang, Marquis Zhi of the Nine Gates, and the rest of Lun’s clique were put to death.

sentences.zh: 言之不從，是謂不乂

translations.literal: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.
translations.idiomatic: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.

sentences.zh: 元康九年六月庚子，有桑生東宮西廂，日長尺餘，甲辰枯死。

translations.literal: Yuankang 9, sixth month, gengzi — a mulberry grew in the western wing of the Eastern Palace, lengthening more than a chi each day; on jiachen it withered and died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi in the sixth month of Yuankang 9, a mulberry shot up in the Eastern Palace’s west wing, grew more than a chi a day, and died on jiachen.

sentences.zh: 此與殷太戊同妖，太子不能悟，故至廢戮也。

translations.literal: This matches Yin emperor Taiwu's portent; the heir could not understand — hence deposition and slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Like Shang precedent, the crown prince ignored the sign.

sentences.zh: 班固稱「野木生朝而暴長，小人將暴居大臣之位，危國亡家之象，朝將為墟也。」

translations.literal: Ban Gu said: "Wild wood in court growing wildly means petty men will usurp ministers' seats — image of state ruin; the court will be waste."
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu said: "Wild wood in court growing wildly means petty men will usurp ministers' seats — image of state ruin; the court will be waste."

sentences.zh: 是後孫秀、張林用事，遂至大亂。

translations.literal: Thereafter Sun Xiu and Zhang Lin held power until great chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Nanfeng's minions fulfilled it.

sentences.zh: 夫乾坤定位，男女流形，伉儷之義同歸，貴賤之名異等。

translations.literal: As for Qian and Kun taking their positions, male and female receive their forms; the principle of husband and wife aims at the same end, yet the names of noble and base stand in different ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth fixed their stations; men and women took their bodily shapes. Husband and wife share one moral purpose, even though rank divides high from low.

sentences.zh: 若乃作配皇極，齊體紫宸，象玉床之連後星，喻金波之合羲璧。

translations.literal: When one is paired with the supreme apex and shares the substance of the Purple Palace, it is likened to the jade couch linking to the rear stars, and compared to golden waves joining the Xi disk.
translations.idiomatic: Those who match the sovereign on high and share the body politic of the inner palace are figured as the jade couch tied to the queen’s asterism, as moonlight married to the solar disk.

sentences.zh: 爰自敻古，是謂元妃；

translations.literal: From remote antiquity onward, she was called the chief consort;
translations.idiomatic: In deepest antiquity she was known as the principal wife;

sentences.zh: 降及中年，乃稱王后。

translations.literal: Descending to middle antiquity, she was then titled queen.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages styled her queen.

sentences.zh: 四人並列，光于帝嚳之宮；

translations.literal: Four women stood ranked together, shining in the palace of Emperor Ku;
translations.idiomatic: Four consorts stood side by side and brought glory to Emperor Ku’s inner court;

sentences.zh: 二妃同降，著彼有虞之典。

translations.literal: Two consorts descended together, written into the canons of Yu’s age.
translations.idiomatic: Two royal brides arrived together and entered the canonical record of Shun’s reign.

sentences.zh: 夏商以上，六宮之制，其詳靡得而聞焉。

translations.literal: Above Xia and Shang, the regulations of the Six Palaces cannot be heard of in detail.
translations.idiomatic: For ages before Xia and Shang, no reliable detail survives about how the six wings of the harem were ordered.

sentences.zh: 姬劉以降，五翟之規，其事可略而言矣。

translations.literal: From Ji and Liu onward, the rules of the five pheasant insignia may be spoken of in outline.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhou and Han dynasties on, the graded “five pheasant” ritual for consorts can at least be sketched.

sentences.zh: 周禮，天子立一后、三夫人、九嬪、二十七世婦、八十一御妻，以聽王者內政。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Son of Heaven establishes one queen, three ladies, nine bin, twenty-seven wives of rank, and eighty-one minor wives, to administer the king’s inner administration.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou prescribe one empress, three chief consorts, nine ranked ladies, twenty-seven secondary wives, and eighty-one attendants to manage the sovereign’s domestic government.

sentences.zh: 故婚義曰：「天子之與后，如日之與月，陰之與陽。」

translations.literal: Therefore the Meaning of Marriage says: “The Son of Heaven and the queen are like sun and moon, yin and yang.”
translations.idiomatic: The Meaning of Marriage therefore declares: “The emperor and his empress mirror sun and moon, yin and yang.”

sentences.zh: 由斯而談，其所從來遠矣。

translations.literal: From this perspective, what they derive from is distant indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by such language, their institution reaches far back into antiquity.

sentences.zh: 故能母儀天宇，助宣王化，德均載物，比大坤維，宗廟歆其薦羞，穹壤俟其交泰。

translations.literal: Thus she can be the motherly model for all under heaven, aid in spreading royal transformation, her virtue evenly bearing all things, comparable to the great sustaining power of Kun; the ancestral temple delights in her offerings, heaven and earth await her harmonizing union.
translations.idiomatic: Hence she sets the maternal standard for the realm, advances the king’s civilizing work, and bears creation as steadfastly as earth itself; the temple accepts her sacrifices gladly, and heaven and earth look to her union with the throne for peace.

sentences.zh: 是以哲王垂憲，尤重造舟之禮；

translations.literal: Therefore wise kings hang forth statutes and especially esteem the rite of the built bridge;
translations.idiomatic: That is why enlightened monarchs codify law and prize above all the royal wedding rite of “meeting across the boat.”

sentences.zh: 詩人立言，先獎葛覃之訓。

translations.literal: The poets set forth words and first praise the instruction of “Ge Tan.”
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry opens by honoring the lessons of “Ge Tan,” the ode on diligent royal ladies.

sentences.zh: 後燭流景，所以裁其宴私；

translations.literal: The rear candle’s flowing light is the means to regulate their private banquets;
translations.idiomatic: Dimming the late-night lamp curbs excess in the privy chamber;

sentences.zh: 房樂希聲，是用節其容止。

translations.literal: Chamber music with sparse sound is the means to moderate their bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Sparse music in the inner rooms reins in conduct at court and couch alike.

sentences.zh: 履端正本，抑斯之謂歟！

translations.literal: Walking upright to rectify the root—is this not what is meant!
translations.idiomatic: Walking straight to set the root right—surely this is what those measures intend!

sentences.zh: 若乃娉納有方，防閑有禮，肅尊儀而修四德，體柔範而弘六義，陰教洽于宮闈，淑譽騰於區域。

translations.literal: If betrothal and intake have proper method, fences and restraint have ritual, reverently honoring ceremony while cultivating the four virtues, embodying gentle norms while extending the six meanings, then women’s instruction permeates the palace, and good reputation rises through the regions.
translations.idiomatic: When matches are arranged by rule, propriety fences passion, majesty guards ritual while the four womanly virtues are cultivated, gentle models enlarge the six canonical lessons, inner-chamber teaching fills the harem, and fair fame spreads beyond the capital.

sentences.zh: 則玄雲入戶，上帝錫母萌之符；

translations.literal: Then dark clouds enter the door, and the Supreme Lord grants the sign of motherhood’s sprouting;
translations.idiomatic: Then auspicious clouds cross the threshold and Heaven grants the token of fruitful motherhood;

sentences.zh: 黃神降徵，坤靈贊壽丘之道，終能鼎祚惟永，胤嗣克昌。

translations.literal: The Yellow Spirit sends down omens; the spirit of Kun assists the way of Shouqiu; ultimately the tripod fortune can be everlasting and heirs flourish.
translations.idiomatic: The divine Yellow Emperor sends portents; earth’s spirit blesses the birth-hill of sage-kings; the dynasty’s mandate endures and heirs thrive.

sentences.zh: 至若儷極虧閑，憑天作孽，倒裳衣于衽席，感朓側於弦望。

translations.literal: As for those paired to the apex yet deficient in restraint, who rely on heaven to work calamity, who overturn upper and lower garments upon the mat, and feel lust askew at first quarter and full moon.
translations.idiomatic: But women who reach the throne yet abandon modesty, who invoke Heaven while plotting harm, who turn proper dress upside down on the bed, and whose passions shift with every phase of the moon—

sentences.zh: 則龍漦結釁，宗周鞠為黍苗；

translations.literal: Then dragon-spittle knots disaster, and royal Zhou becomes nothing but millet shoots;
translations.idiomatic: —dragon spit seals a fatal feud, and the Zhou heartland turns to weed-grown ruin;

sentences.zh: 燕尾挻災，隆漢墜其枌社矣。

translations.literal: Swallow tails draw calamity, and flourishing Han drops its mulberry altars.
translations.idiomatic: swallow-tail charms invite catastrophe, and even mighty Han loses its soil-and-millet shrines.

sentences.zh: 自曹劉內主，位以色登，甄衛之家，榮非德舉。

translations.literal: Since the inner mistresses of Cao and Liu, position climbed by beauty; in the households of Zhen and Wei, glory was not raised by virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Cao and Liu courts, palace ladies rose by looks alone; clans such as the Zhens and Weis won favor without moral merit.

sentences.zh: 淫荒挺性，蔑西郊之禮容；

translations.literal: Dissolute and wasteful by nature, they slighted the ritual bearing of the western suburb;
translations.idiomatic: Wanton temperaments mocked the solemn suburban liturgy reserved for the empress;

sentences.zh: 婉孌含辭，作南國之奇態。

translations.literal: Soft loveliness holding coy phrases, they fashioned exotic manners of the southern states.
translations.idiomatic: Soft voices and studied phrases invented the freakish grace of southern entertainers.

sentences.zh: 詖謁由斯外人，穢德於是內宣。

translations.literal: Slanderous flattery thereby passed outward, and foul conduct was proclaimed within.
translations.idiomatic: Sycophancy leaked beyond the palace gates while depravity was preached inside.

sentences.zh: 椒掖播晨牝之風，蘭殿絕河雎之響。

translations.literal: The pepper chambers spread the wind of the hen crowing at dawn; the orchid halls cut off the echo of “Guan ju” by the River.
translations.idiomatic: The harem aired the omen of women ruling like crowing hens; orchid halls no longer echoed the chaste songs of “Guan ju.”

sentences.zh: 永言彤史，大練之範逾微；

translations.literal: Speaking long of the vermilion scribe, the model of coarse white silk grows ever fainter;
translations.idiomatic: Forever the palace diarists wrote, yet the ideal of homespun austerity faded;

sentences.zh: 緬視青蒲，脫珥之猷替矣。

translations.literal: Gazing afar at the green rushes, the strategy of casting off ear-jewels is replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back to mat audiences where consorts remonstrated, the counsel of tearing off earrings to warn the throne had vanished.

sentences.zh: 晉承其末，與世污隆，宣皇創基，功弘而道屈；

translations.literal: Jin inherited the late age; with the world it sank and rose. Emperor Xuan founded the base—achievement broad yet the Way bent;
translations.idiomatic: The Jin took up this fallen era and rose or fell with the times. Emperor Xuan laid the foundations: his deeds were grand, yet the moral course stayed cramped;

sentences.zh: 穆后一善，勣侔於十亂。

translations.literal: one goodness of Empress Mu—merit equal to the Ten Disorderly Ones.
translations.idiomatic: a single virtue in Empress Mu rivaled the merit of the “ten turbulent” worthies who saved a dynasty.

sentences.zh: 洎乎世祖，[1]始親選良家，既而帝掩紈扇，躬行請託。

translations.literal: Down to Shizu [1], he began personally selecting from good families; thereafter the emperor hid behind the silk fan and personally practiced solicitation.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu [1] the court at first picked brides from respectable houses; soon the sovereign waved his silk fan in the inner quarters and himself traded favors for appointments.

sentences.zh: 后採長白，實彰妒忌之情；

translations.literal: The empress chose “long white,” truly displaying jealousy;
translations.idiomatic: An empress chosen for graying hair laid bare the spite of jealousy;

sentences.zh: 賈納短青，竟踐覆亡之轍。

translations.literal: Jia took in “short green,” and in the end trod the rut of overthrow.
translations.idiomatic: the Jias welcomed a young rival and eventually followed the same rut to ruin.

sentences.zh: 得失遺跡，煥在綈緗，興滅所由，義同畫一。

translations.literal: Tracks of gain and loss shine forth on silk documents; the causes of rise and ruin share one uniform pattern in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Success and failure still gleam from the silk-bound histories; the springs of fortune and disaster follow one clear pattern.

sentences.zh: 故列其本事，以為后妃傳云。

translations.literal: Therefore I array their basic affairs to form this treatise on empresses and consorts.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore set out the essential facts as this “Treatise on Empresses and Consorts.”

sentences.zh: 及太子廢黜，趙王倫、孫秀等因眾怨謀欲廢后[8]。

translations.literal: When crown prince deposed—Prince Zhao Lun and Sun Xiu exploiting resentment plotted depose consort [8].
translations.idiomatic: Once Minhuai fell Sima Lun and Sun Xiu used hatred to target her [8].

sentences.zh: 后數遣宮婢微服於人間視聽，其謀頗泄。

translations.literal: Consort repeatedly sent palace maids plain clothes among folk spy listen—plot leaked somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: She spied on rumors—some leaked.

sentences.zh: 后甚懼，遂害太子，以絕眾望。

translations.literal: Consort greatly afraid—thereupon harmed crown prince—cutting off hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified she murdered Minhuai.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫乃率兵入宮，使翊軍校尉齊王冏入殿廢后。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Lun then led troops palace—ordered Colonel Qi Wang Jiong enter hall depose consort.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun stormed in—sent Sima Jiong to drag her out.

sentences.zh: 后與冏母有隙，故倫使之。

translations.literal: Consort with Jiong’s mother bore grudge—therefore Lun sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong hated her mother—Lun used him.

sentences.zh: 后驚曰：「卿何為來！」

translations.literal: Consort alarmed said: “Why have you come!”
translations.idiomatic: She cried, “Why you!”

sentences.zh: 冏曰：「有詔收后。」

translations.literal: Jiong said: "There is an edict to seize you."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong said, "There is an edict to seize you."

sentences.zh: 后曰：「詔當從我出，何詔也？」

translations.literal: Consort said: "Edicts issue from me—what edict is this?"
translations.idiomatic: She snapped, "Edicts issue from me—what edict is this?"

sentences.zh: 后至上閤，遙呼帝曰：「陛下有婦，使人廢之，亦行自廢。」

translations.literal: Consort reaching upper chamber cried distant emperor: “Your Majesty has wife yet lets others depose her—you yourself will be deposed.”
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the upper chamber she cried to the emperor, "Your Majesty has a wife, yet you let others depose her—you will be deposed yourself."

sentences.zh: 又問冏曰：「起事者誰？」

translations.literal: Again asked Jiong: “Who raised revolt?”
translations.idiomatic: She asked Jiong again, "Who raised this affair?"

sentences.zh: 冏曰：「梁、趙。」

translations.literal: Jiong said: “Liang and Zhao.”
translations.idiomatic: “Liang and Zhao.”

sentences.zh: 后曰：「繫狗當繫頸，今反繫其尾，何得不然！」

translations.literal: Consort said: “Leash dog by throat—now leash tail—how can it not be so!”
translations.idiomatic: “Chain a dog by the throat—you seized the tail—no wonder!”

sentences.zh: 至宮西，見謐尸，再舉聲而哭遽止。

translations.literal: Reaching palace west saw Mi corpse—raised voice twice weeping suddenly stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Jia Mi’s corpse she wailed twice—then silence.

sentences.zh: 倫乃矯詔遣尚書劉弘等持節齎金屑酒賜后死。

translations.literal: Lun then forged edict dispatch Minister Liu Hong bearing tally deliver gold-filings wine grant consort death.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun sent Liu Hong with golden liquor.

sentences.zh: 后在位十一年。

translations.literal: Consort held rank eleven years.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven years queen.

sentences.zh: 趙粲、賈午、韓壽、董猛等皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Zhao Can, Jia Wu, Han Shou, Dong Meng executed.
translations.idiomatic: Her cabal died with her.

sentences.zh: 惠羊皇后諱獻容，泰山南城人。

translations.literal: Empress Yang of Hui, taboo Xianrong, native of Nancheng in Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang Xianrong came from Nancheng in Taishan.

sentences.zh: 祖瑾，父玄之，並見外戚傳。

translations.literal: Grandfather Jin; father Xuanzhi—both treated in Outer Kin treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Yang Jin and father Yang Xuanzhi appear among outer kin.

sentences.zh: 賈后既廢，孫秀議立后。

translations.literal: After Empress Jia deposed—Sun Xiu debated establishing empress.
translations.idiomatic: After Jia Nanfeng fell Sun Xiu debated a new queen.

sentences.zh: 后外祖孫旂與秀合族，又諸子自結於秀，故以太安元年立為皇后[9]。

translations.literal: Consort maternal grandfather Sun Qi shared clan with Xiu—sons bonded with Xiu—therefore first Taian year established empress [9].
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qi’s tie to Sun Xiu won her the throne in 302 [9].

sentences.zh: 將入宮，衣中有火。

translations.literal: About to enter palace—fire appeared within robes.
translations.idiomatic: Fire sparked inside her robes on palace entry.

sentences.zh: 傅玄

translations.literal: Fu Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan

sentences.zh: 倫篡，又為右光祿、開府，加侍中。

translations.literal: When Lun usurped, he again was right grand master of splendid horses, established office, added palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun seized the throne, Fu Zhi became right grand master of splendid horses with independent establishment and added palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 惠帝還宮，祗以經受偽職請退，不許。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui returned to the palace, Zhi because he had received illicit office asked to retire—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Hui returned, Fu Zhi asked to resign for having served the usurper; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 初，倫之篡也，孫秀與義陽王威等十餘人預撰儀式禪文。

translations.literal: At first when Lun usurped, Sun Xiu and Prince of Yiyang, Wei, and more than a dozen others pre-drafted the ceremonies and abdication texts.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun first usurped, Sun Xiu, Prince Yiyang Sima Wei, and a dozen others had drafted the abdication liturgy and text.

sentences.zh: 及倫敗，齊王冏收侍中劉逵、常侍騶捷、杜育、黃門郎陸機、右丞周導、王尊等付廷尉。

translations.literal: When Lun fell, the prince of Qi, Jiong, seized palace attendant Liu Dai, regular attendants Zou Jie, Du Yu, yellow gate gentleman Lu Ji, right aide Zhou Dao, Wang Zun, and others and handed them to the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun fell, Prince Qi Sima Jiong arrested Liu Dai, Zou Jie, Du Yu, Lu Ji, Zhou Dao, Wang Zun, and others for the commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 以禪文出中書，復議處祗罪，會赦得原。

translations.literal: Because the abdication text came from the secretariat, they again debated punishing Zhi's crime, but a general amnesty arrived and he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Because the abdication edict had issued from the secretariat, some wanted Fu Zhi punished, but a general amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 後以禪文草本非祗所撰，於是詔復光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later because the abdication draft in manuscript was not written by Zhi, thereupon an edict restored him as grand counsellor of splendid horses.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was shown the draft was not his hand, and an edict restored him as grand counsellor of splendid horses.

sentences.zh: 子宣，尚弘農公主。

translations.literal: His son Xuan married the Princess of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu Xuan married the princess of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 愍懷太子

translations.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai
